email.description: The contact address the request arrived from. Records are located by it, canonically (trimmed and lower-cased).

store.description: One store in the enumerated erasure scope. The scope is enumerated in exactly one place so a store added later cannot be silently skipped.

tables.description: The database tables that store covers.

disposition.description: What was done. `retained`, `not_applicable` and `failed` always carry a reason.

records_affected.description: How many records the disposition applied to: deleted, anonymized, or counted and kept. Zero for a not-applicable or failed store.

reason.description: Why the records were kept, why the store held nothing reachable, or why it failed.

ErasureRequest.description:
A recorded erasure request, its acknowledgement and — once processed — the outcome per store.
It deliberately carries NO field naming the person: not the member id it was recorded against, not the contact address. The acknowledgement goes back to whoever already proved they are that person, so echoing it would only make the response another copy of what the request exists to erase. The stored record itself is cleared of both the moment processing completes.

origin.description: `member` for an authenticated in-product request, `contact` for one recorded by an operator on behalf of a person with no account.

status.description: `received` is recorded and awaiting processing. `completed` is every store visited without failure, with the identifying input cleared. `refused` is nothing erased, with `refusal_reason` saying what must happen first. `failed` is at least one store that could not be processed, kept retryable.

acknowledgement.description: The plain-language acknowledgement, stating the processing window while the request is open.

respond_by.description: The deadline of the stated processing window, persisted when the request was recorded so a later configuration change cannot move a commitment already made.

response_window_days.description: The stated window in days, derived from this request's own timestamps.

processed_at.description: When the request finished processing, or null while still pending.

refusal_reason.description: Present only for a refused request: what must happen first, and the options available.

outcomes.description: One entry per enumerated store, in registry order.

report.description: The rendered, human-readable report naming what was deleted, what was anonymized and what was retained with the reason for each. Empty until the request has been processed.

payload.description: The event's JSON document. Its shape varies by event_type; it is an opaque, schema-less record of what happened.

actor.description: Who or what triggered the recorded mutation. Omitted for an event recorded by a module that has not adopted attribution yet (predates_actor_capture is false in that case) or for an event that predates actor attribution entirely (predates_actor_capture is true) — an absent actor is never defaulted to a specific value.

predates_actor_capture.description: True only for an event recorded before this platform captured actors at all. Distinguishes that historical gap from an event recorded afterward whose actor is absent because the recording module has not adopted attribution yet — the latter is a defect to fix, the former is not.

type.description: member is an authenticated Member acting through a self-serve surface, staff is a platform StaffMember acting across Organizations through a staff-only surface (e.g. issuing a refund), system is the platform's own scheduled processing (e.g. renewal), and gateway is an inbound payment-gateway webhook.

id.description: The acting Member's or StaffMember's id. Present only for a member or staff actor; a system or gateway actor carries none.

limit.description: The pagination limit actually applied (default when none supplied).

has_more.description: Whether at least one further audit event exists beyond this page. Always false for an unbounded export request, since nothing was capped. A response never presents a subset as if it were the whole.

limit.description: The pagination limit actually applied (default when none supplied).
The pagination limit actually applied (default when none supplied).

has_more.description: Whether at least one further feature flag exists beyond this page. A response never presents a subset as if it were the whole.

limit.description: The pagination limit actually applied (default when none supplied).

name.description: A closed set. An event named anything else is rejected, so the value can never become unbounded and visitor-controlled.

route.description: A pathname only, already normalized to its route template by the client. A value carrying a query string or fragment is rejected rather than truncated.

properties.description: At most 10 entries, keys drawn from a closed allowlist. Values containing an "@" are rejected, so this cannot become a channel for personal data.

visitor_id.description: A pseudonymous, browser-generated opaque token. Never derived from an IP address, user agent, email or anything else that would identify the visitor across sites.

policy_version.description: The cookie-policy version the decision was made against.

accepted.description: Whether the submission was queued. It is false both when the queue is saturated and when the submission was discarded for lack of consent — deliberately, so the caller learns nothing about stored state.

visitors.description: Distinct visitors in this bucket, counted once each.

locale.description: The marketing-site locale the lead was submitted from, inferred by the client from the page's route.

visitor_session_id.description: The submitting browser's pseudonymous visitor id, sent only when the visitor granted analytics consent. Optional: a submission without it is equally valid, and stitching the Lead to that visitor's journey never affects whether the Lead is persisted.

source.description: The specific page or tool that captured this lead (e.g. "pricing_page", "migration_checker"), distinct from landing_url. Optional.

disposition.description: Staff's recorded outcome of working this Lead. `new` until a staff member with `leads:work` records one.

region.description: The declared data-residency region. The accepted set is the set of regions this deployment actually serves, taken from its `SERVED_REGIONS` configuration — not from this enumeration, which mirrors it. This deployment serves `us` only: every byte is stored in one Amazon Web Services United States region. A recognized region it does not serve (for example `eu`) is refused with `organization_region_not_served` rather than accepted and quietly stored elsewhere.

The data-residency region this Organization declared when it was created. It is immutable. The set accepted at creation is narrower than the set readable here: an Organization created before a region was withdrawn still carries it, and those are listed for reconciliation at `GET /v1/staff/organizations/unserved-regions`. A region here is a declared and audited commitment, not one enforced by separate regional infrastructure — this deployment stores all data in one Amazon Web Services United States region.

UnservedRegionOrganizationsResponse.description: One page of Organizations declaring a data-residency region this deployment does not serve, for operator reconciliation.

total.description: The number of matching Organizations across the whole table, not just this page, so a capped page discloses what it left behind.

served_regions.description: The regions this deployment actually serves, which is what membership of this listing was measured against.

CreateOrganizationResponse.description: An Organization plus its single-use identity-provider bootstrap credential, returned in plaintext exactly once and never retrievable again.

region.description: The data-residency region assigned to the new Organization. See the `Organization` schema's own `region` for what the commitment means and where the data actually lives.

identity_provider_bootstrap_token.description: Single-use, 30-minute credential authorizing exactly one call to PUT /v1/organizations/{organization_id}/identity-provider before the Organization has any Member.

skipped.description: Every FeatureFlag whose configuration could not be copied, named explicitly rather than failing the clone silently.

is_production.description: Whether this environment is marked as production. Explicit, operator-set state, never inferred from name or slug — surfaces that require proportional confirmation before a destructive or high-impact action (e.g. the kill switch) read this field.

requires_approval.description: Whether a manual EnvironmentFlagConfig write to this environment is refused pending approval.

disable_exempt_from_approval.description: Whether the distinct kill-switch (disable) operation bypasses requires_approval. Only meaningful when requires_approval is true; defaults to true so a newly-gated environment never silently blocks its own kill switch.

key.description: Optional. A feature flag's key is immutable after creation: if supplied, it MUST equal the flag's current key, or the request is refused with feature_flag_key_immutable. Omit this field entirely on a routine rename.

tags.description: Optional. When present, replaces the flag's tags wholesale. Omit this field entirely to leave existing tags untouched.

archived_at.description: When the feature flag was archived, or null when it is active. Archiving is a soft state: the flag, its variations and all of its history remain readable, only its entitlement slot is released and its targeting disabled everywhere.

attribute.description: Mutually exclusive with segment_id. Both attribute and value set is a clause condition; both empty (with no segment_id) is an unconditional catch-all.

op.description: The clause operator, from expand-targeting-model's enumerated, closed set. Omitted defaults to eq (exact string equality), matching every Rule authored before this field existed.

value_type.description: The typed shape value carries. Omitted defaults to string, matching every Rule authored before this field existed.

segment_id.description: References an existing Segment's conditions instead of an inline attribute/value pair. Mutually exclusive with attribute.

condition.description: expand-targeting-model's composed condition (AND/OR/negation/ nesting) — mutually exclusive with attribute/segment_id. Omitted means this Rule uses the flat leaf shape above instead.

ClauseTree.description: A rule condition node: a single leaf clause, or a group of child clause_trees combined with AND/OR, or a negation of exactly one child, per environment-flag-targeting's "Clauses Compose With AND, OR And Negation" requirement. Groups nest to a bounded depth (5, expand-targeting-model task 1.2's recorded bound). Mirrors apps/api/internal/evaluation/domain's ClauseTree JSON encoding exactly — there is one wire shape, not two independently-drifting ones.

attribute.description: Set only for a leaf node.

type.description: Set only for a leaf node.

value.description: Set only for a leaf node; its shape follows type.

clause.description: Set only for a "not" node — the single negated child.

PutEnvironmentFlagConfigResponse.description: Discriminated by status: "applied" nests the resulting environment_flag_config (the write took effect immediately, as before governance change control existed); "pending_approval" instead carries pending_approval_request_id -- the owning Environment requires approval and the change is held rather than applied.

id.description: Present only for a member or staff actor.

configuration.description: The resulting configuration's targeting-model snapshot, the same shape as EnvironmentFlagConfig's own enabled/ default_variation_id/rules fields.

restored_from_point_id.description: Present only when this point is the result of a restore: the id of the history point it restored.

promoted_from_environment_id.description: Present only when this point is the result of a promotion: the id of the source environment.

has_more.description: True when more history points exist beyond this page.

presence.description: "before_only"/"after_only" means the rule at this position exists on only one side, per flag-change-history's "A construct is present on one side only" scenario.

identical.description: True when the two compared configurations are identical. Explicit rather than inferred from empty fields/rules arrays, per flag-change-history's "The configurations are identical" scenario.

presence.description: "before_only"/"after_only" means the flag is configured in only one of the two compared environments.

paused_by.description: Who initiated the current pause. Present only while state is paused; absent otherwise. A guardrail-initiated pause is eligible for automatic resume once that Guardrail is no longer sustained-uncertain; an operator-initiated pause only resumes via an explicit resume call.

last_applied_stage_position.description: -1 when no stage has been applied yet.

evaluation_window_seconds.description: Must be positive. The window of Observations averaged at evaluation time, ending at the evaluation instant.

promote_after_healthy_seconds.description: Optional. Must be positive when set. Once this Guardrail has been continuously healthy for at least this duration, it triggers an early promotion of the owning Rollout's next Stage. Omitted entirely means this Guardrail does not participate in promotion.

pause_after_uncertain_seconds.description: Optional. Must be positive when set. Once this Guardrail has been continuously insufficient-data for at least this duration, it pauses the owning Rollout. Omitted entirely means this Guardrail does not participate in pausing.

resume_cool_down_seconds.description: Optional. Must be positive when set. After this Guardrail automatically resumes a Rollout it paused, it will not automatically re-pause for sustained-uncertain metrics again until this duration has elapsed. Never suppresses an automatic rollback caused by a breached metric. Omitted entirely means no cool-down.

promote_after_healthy_seconds.description: Absent when this Guardrail does not participate in promotion.

pause_after_uncertain_seconds.description: Absent when this Guardrail does not participate in pausing.

resume_cool_down_seconds.description: Absent when this Guardrail has no resume cool-down.

promote_after_healthy_seconds.description: Absent when this GuardrailTemplate does not participate in promotion.

pause_after_uncertain_seconds.description: Absent when this GuardrailTemplate does not participate in pausing.

resume_cool_down_seconds.description: Absent when this GuardrailTemplate has no resume cool-down.

review_status.description: Starts draft on creation. Must be approved before the template can be installed onto a Rollout. Any wholesale Update reverts it to draft.

rejection_reason.description: Present only when review_status is rejected.

note.description: Optional reviewer comment. Accepted but not persisted.

MappingRequest.description: The request body shared by creating and editing a ContractTemplateVersion's mapping.

rejection_reason.description: Present only when review_status is rejected.

template_id.description: The ContractTemplate this Connector's mapping comes from — either platform-scoped (usable by any Project) or project-scoped and owned by this same Project.

template_version.description: Optional. Pins the Connector to a specific, approved version of template_id. Omitted resolves to template_id's highest currently approved version at creation time. Immutable after creation except via an explicit later edit — see UpdateConnectorRequest.

source_url.description: Must be an https URL. It is parsed and its scheme is checked, so a value that merely begins with "https" but is not a valid https URL is refused. The pull secret is presented to this URL as a bearer credential on every sync, so a plaintext destination is never accepted.

template_id.description: Optional. Omitted keeps the Connector's current template reference unchanged. Supplying a different (template_id, template_version) than the Connector currently has is the only way to recover a `broken` Connector to `active`.

template_version.description: Optional. Only consulted when template_id is also supplied; omitted then resolves to template_id's highest currently approved version.

source_url.description: Must be an https URL, checked the same way CreateConnectorRequest.source_url is.

secret.description: Optional. A non-empty value rotates the pull secret; omitted or empty leaves the existing secret untouched.

source_url.description: Must be an https URL, checked the same way CreateConnectorRequest.source_url is.

secret.description: Optional. Sent as a Bearer token to source_url, same as a Connector's own pull secret.

raw_response.description: The raw, JSON-parsed response fetched from source_url.

observations.description: The Observations the mapping produces from raw_response. Absent when error is present.

error.description: Present instead of observations when the mapping fails to resolve against raw_response (e.g. a field path not found). raw_response is still returned in this case.

template_version.description: The version of template_id's mapping this Connector is pinned to. Changes only via an explicit edit.

secret.description: Never present here — the sibling `not` requirement excludes it. Declared only so that requirement references a defined property; see ConnectorCreated for when a response actually carries the plaintext secret.

last_sync_status.description: Absent when this Connector has never been synced.

last_sync_at.description: Absent when this Connector has never been synced.

last_sync_error.description: Absent on success or when this Connector has never been synced.

last_sync_failure_kind.description: Absent on success or when this Connector has never been synced. Only mapping_mismatch counts toward the automatic circuit breaker that transitions status to broken. insecure_destination means this Connector's source_url is not an https URL: it was configured before that was required, and no sync will present the pull secret to it until the source_url is corrected.

last_sync_observation_count.description: Absent when this Connector has never synced successfully.

consecutive_mapping_mismatches.description: Consecutive mapping_mismatch failures. Resets to zero on a successful sync; a transient failure leaves it unchanged. Reaching 3 transitions status to broken.

template_version.description: The version of template_id's mapping this Connector is pinned to. Changes only via an explicit edit.

secret.description: The plaintext pull secret. Returned only in the creation response, or an update response that rotated it; no other response ever includes it.

last_sync_status.description: Absent when this Connector has never been synced.

last_sync_at.description: Absent when this Connector has never been synced.

last_sync_error.description: Absent on success or when this Connector has never been synced.

last_sync_failure_kind.description: Absent on success or when this Connector has never been synced. Only mapping_mismatch counts toward the automatic circuit breaker that transitions status to broken. insecure_destination means this Connector's source_url is not an https URL: it was configured before that was required, and no sync will present the pull secret to it until the source_url is corrected.

last_sync_observation_count.description: Absent when this Connector has never synced successfully.

consecutive_mapping_mismatches.description: Consecutive mapping_mismatch failures. Resets to zero on a successful sync; a transient failure leaves it unchanged. Reaching 3 transitions status to broken.

reason.description: Explicit human-readable reason, populated for insufficient-data (no Observations in the window), already-handled (breached, but a sibling Guardrail's breach already aborted the Rollout in the same tick), sustained-healthy (promoted), sustained- uncertain (paused), and no-longer-uncertain (resumed) evaluations; empty otherwise.

variation_ids.description: Must be at least two ids, all belonging to the FeatureFlag, with no duplicates.

winning_variation_id.description: Optional. Must be one of the Experiment's own compared variation_ids.

conclusion.description: Absent (empty) until the Experiment is concluded.

winning_variation_id.description: Present only if a winning Variation was declared at conclusion.

started_at.description: Present only once the Experiment has been started.

concluded_at.description: Present only once the Experiment has been concluded.

insufficient_data.description: True when any compared Variation has zero distinct attributed subjects. When true, variations/statistic/p_value/ mismatch_detected are all absent: no computed statistic exists in that case.

variations.description: Present only when insufficient_data is false.

statistic.description: The chi-squared goodness-of-fit statistic. Present only when insufficient_data is false.

p_value.description: The approximate p-value, via the Wilson-Hilferty transformation. Present only when insufficient_data is false.

mismatch_detected.description: True iff p_value is below the fixed significance threshold (p < 0.001). Present only when insufficient_data is false.

effect_size.description: Difference of proportions (count metrics) or difference of means (sum/average/rate metrics), variation minus baseline.

p_value.description: Two-tailed p-value. No significance verdict is included; the operator interprets effect_size, the confidence interval and p_value together.

unassigned_subject_count.description: Subjects with no attributed exposure to one of the Experiment's own compared Variations.

contaminated_subject_count.description: Subjects whose attributed exposures span more than one of the Experiment's own compared Variations.

multiple_comparison_correction_applied.description: Always false in this iteration; disclosed explicitly rather than hidden when more than two Variations are compared.

resolved.description: False when no AcquisitionContext could be resolved for the subjects in this bucket, by direct match or either single-hop identity resolution — distinct from a resolved AcquisitionContext whose UTM fields happen to be blank.

public.description: Issue this credential as safe to embed in browser-visible code. MUST be restricted to exactly the config:read scope — issuing a Public credential with any other scope is rejected. Defaults to false.

name.description: Optional human-readable label, so an operator can tell two credentials apart in the listing. Omitted means unnamed.

expires_at.description: Optional instant at which this credential stops authenticating requests. Omitted means it never expires. An expired credential is refused exactly like an unknown one.

public.description: Whether this credential was issued as safe to embed in browser-visible code. Fixed at issuance.

token.description: The plaintext credential token. Returned only in the issuance response; no other response ever includes it.

name.description: The human-readable label supplied at issue time. Absent when the credential is unnamed.

expires_at.description: The instant this credential stops authenticating requests. Absent when it never expires.

InviteMemberRequest.description: Carries the invited email and the role they will hold on acceptance. There is deliberately no organization_id field: an invite is always issued into the caller's own session-bound Organization, so the body cannot express a cross-tenant issuance. Unknown fields are rejected.

role.description: The role the invitee will hold once this invite is accepted. Omitted or empty defaults to the base "member" role. Conferring any other role requires the inviter to themselves hold roles:manage; conferring one that includes role administration follows the same approval rule as granting it directly.

MemberInviteResponse.description: A MemberInvite projected for administration. It has no token field by design: only the emailed link ever carries the accept token, and only a one-way hash of it is persisted.

status.description: The status an operator must act on. A pending invite whose expiry has lapsed is reported as expired even though the stored row still says pending.

AcceptInviteResponse.description: The Member provisioned by a successful acceptance. It has no session-token field: accepting an invite provisions a Member, it does not sign anybody in.

pending_approval_request_id.description: Set only when the invite's role included role administration: the Member above is provisioned, but the role grant itself awaits a second member's approval.

session_token.description: The plaintext session token. Returned only in this response; no other response ever includes it.

RequestMagicLinkResponse.description: Deliberately identical whether or not the email matched an existing Member — see requestMagicLink's description.

RequestStaffMagicLinkResponse.description: Deliberately identical whether or not the email matched an active StaffMember — see requestStaffMagicLink's description.

PeekStaffMagicLinkResponse.description: Reports validity only. It never names the StaffMember the token belongs to.

StaffMember.description: A platform-staff identity. It has no organization field by design: a StaffMember acts across every Organization and is a distinct identity from a Member, even when the same email also holds a Member account somewhere. It carries no token or hash field either, so no staff endpoint can leak credential material.

permissions.description: The staff permissions this StaffMember was granted, drawn from a small fixed catalog. Read-only here: granting and revoking are out-of-band operations with no API surface.

ConfirmStaffMagicLinkResponse.description: The only place the plaintext StaffSession token is ever returned; only its one-way hash is persisted.

CurrentStaffSessionResponse.description: The staff identity behind a presented StaffSession. It has no session-token field by design, so the endpoint cannot leak the token it is looked up by.

IssueRefundRequest.description:
A staff-issued refund request against a one-off charge.

It carries no currency: a refund is always denominated in the charge's own currency, which the API reads from the charge itself, so a currency mismatch is impossible rather than merely rejected.

amount.description: The amount to refund, in the charge's currency's smallest unit (e.g. cents). Must be positive and must not exceed the charge's remaining refundable balance.

StaffChargeResponse.description: The refund-facing view of a one-off charge.

StaffCharge.description: A one-off charge as platform staff see it for refund purposes. Every amount is an integer in currency's smallest unit (e.g. cents), never a float.

status.description: The charge's own lifecycle status. A refund never changes it: a fully refunded charge stays `paid`, since a refund is money voluntarily returned, not a payment reversed by the cardholder's bank (which is a dispute, and does move the status to `disputed`). `failed` means the gateway attempted the charge and was declined, as opposed to `expired`, which means an asynchronous method's payment window elapsed with nobody ever attempting to pay it.

refunded_amount.description: How much of this charge the payment gateway has confirmed as refunded so far, across every refund against it. It moves only on a gateway webhook confirmation, never on a refund request, so it can briefly lag a refund just issued.

remaining_refundable_amount.description: `amount` minus `refunded_amount` — how much of this charge is still refundable. Returned rather than left to the caller so the two can never be read inconsistently.

CurrentSessionResponse.description: The identity behind a presented session. It has no session-token field by design, so the endpoint cannot leak the token it is looked up by.

roles.description: The roles this Member holds. Empty for a Member with no role assignment, which is the default after just-in-time provisioning.

terms.description:
The terms of service in force, and whether this Member still owes an acceptance of it. Carried on the identity response rather than on a second endpoint because the operator shell reads this on every authenticated render, and a separate call would let an authenticated screen paint before the answer arrived.

No acceptance timestamp and no previously-accepted version are reported: the client only needs to know whether to ask. The record itself is evidence held server-side.

current_version.description: The version marker of the terms of service currently in force, empty on a deployment that publishes no terms. Clients render this rather than restating a version of their own, so the published document and the accepted version cannot drift apart.

acceptance_required.description: True when this Member's recorded acceptance is for an earlier version or for nothing at all. A Member provisioned by SCIM, by an invite, by just-in-time OIDC login or by social signup starts with no recorded acceptance, so this is true for all of them until they have accepted.

AcceptTermsRequest.description: The version the caller is accepting. It is COMPARED against the version in force, never stored as given: a stale browser cannot record an acceptance of the document it happened to be showing.

GrantRoleResponse.description: Discriminated by status: "granted" carries the created RoleAssignment; "pending_approval" carries approval_request_id instead.

ApprovalRequest.description: Kind discriminates which fields are meaningful: "role_grant" populates target_member_id and role; "environment_flag_config_change" populates environment_id and feature_flag_id instead -- see complete-governance-surface's "Let approvals gate production change."

token.description: Present only in the issuance response — the plaintext token is never retrievable again.

ScimPatchRequest.description: RFC 7644 §3.5.2 PatchOp shape. Only an "active" value is inspected; every other attribute is ignored.

public.description: Whether this credential was issued as safe to embed in browser-visible code. Fixed at issuance.

name.description: The human-readable label supplied at issue time. Absent when the credential is unnamed.

expires_at.description: The instant this credential stops authenticating requests. Absent when it never expires.

last_used_at.description: The instant this credential last authenticated a request. ABSENT means it has never been used — that is how a never-used credential is distinguished from one used at a known instant. Recorded asynchronously, so it may lag a request by seconds.

RotatedCredential.description: A rotated credential: its unchanged metadata, the replacement token (disclosed here once and never again) and the instant the previous secret stops being accepted.

token.description: The plaintext replacement token. Returned only in this rotation response; no other response ever includes it.

previous_secret_expires_at.description: The instant the secret being replaced stops being accepted.

url.description: Must be an https URL. It is parsed and its scheme is checked, so a value that merely begins with "https" but is not a valid https URL is refused.

secret.description: The plaintext signing secret. Returned only in the creation response; no other response ever includes it. Used to compute each delivery's X-Webhook-Signature HMAC-SHA256 header.

limit.description: The pagination limit actually applied (default when none supplied).

has_more.description: Whether at least one further delivery exists beyond this page. A response never presents a subset as if it were the whole.

last_attempted_at.description: Null until the first delivery attempt.

payload.description: The full enveloped body (event_type, event_version, occurred_at, data) that was signed and sent to the receiving endpoint.

last_attempted_at.description: Null until the first delivery attempt.

conditions.description: Attribute-equality conditions that MUST ALL match (logical AND) for this Rule to apply. Absent or empty means an unconditional catch-all. A Rule that referenced a reusable Segment has that Segment's conditions resolved here — the two look identical on the wire. This flat shape is served whenever the Rule's own condition is exactly representable as it (every pre-section-5 Rule, and any composed one that happens to reduce to a flat AND of equality leaves); condition below is served instead when it genuinely needs the composed tree shape.

condition.description: expand-targeting-model's composed condition (AND/OR/negation/ nesting) — served instead of conditions when the Rule's own condition cannot be reduced to that flat shape. See conditions' own description for exactly when each is served.

non_evaluable.description: True when this FlagConfig uses a construct newer than the format version the requesting client declared support for via the X-Rollfuse-Client-Format-Version request header (see Configuration.format_version). When true, variations and rules are empty and MUST NOT be evaluated — the client MUST serve the caller's own fallback for this flag instead, per feature-evaluation's "The Configuration Format Is Versioned For Compatibility" requirement. Omitted (false) for every flag today, since no construct newer than format version 1 exists yet.

version.description: Monotonically increasing Configuration Version for this Environment. Advances whenever a FeatureFlag, its Variations, or an EnvironmentFlagConfig affecting this Environment is created, updated or removed. Also served as GET /v1/config's ETag response header (quoted, e.g. "v3") — a request carrying that value in If-None-Match gets 304 Not Modified with no body instead of a full Configuration.

format_version.description: The highest configuration format version this platform can serve at all today. Informational: it does not by itself indicate whether any individual flag in `flags` was withheld as non_evaluable for the requesting client's own declared version, which may be lower.

poll_interval_seconds.description: Advised interval, in seconds, for a client polling GET /v1/config. Paired with the ETag/If-None-Match support above: a client polling at this interval and presenting its last ETag pays only a 304 on most polls.

flag_key.description: Omit to evaluate every FeatureFlag configured in the Environment.

has_more.description: Whether more ExposureEvents exist beyond this page. Set by GET /v1/environments/{environment_id}/feature-flags/{feature_flag_id}/exposure-events; absent from GET /v1/experiments/{experiment_id}/exposure-events.

correlation_id.description: Client-generated. Falls back to the request's own request id when omitted.

occurred_at.description: When the local evaluation that produced this event occurred. Falls back to the server's receive time when omitted.

accepted.description: How many submitted events resolved to a known flag_key and were handed off for best-effort recording.

archived_at.description: When the metric definition was archived, or null when it is active. Archiving is a soft state: it stops being offered for new use, but every existing Guardrail, Connector or Observation referencing it continues to resolve.

subject_key.description: Optional identifier of who or what generated this observation. Required for the observation to be assignable to a Variation during experiment outcome analysis.

has_more.description: Whether more Observations exist beyond this page. Set by GET /v1/environments/{environment_id}/metric-definitions/{metric_definition_id}/observations and GET /v1/environments/{environment_id}/observations; absent from GET /v1/experiments/{experiment_id}/observations.

plan_version_id.description: The specific immutable PlanVersion in play. A Subscription is always pinned to a version, never to the catalog entry, so editing the catalog never silently changes an existing subscriber's terms.

amount.description: An integer amount in the smallest unit of currency (e.g. cents), never a float. May be 0 — the platform's default plan is a $0 plan.

effective_at.description: When the agreed change takes financial and entitlement effect — the end of the current billing cycle, for a downgrade.

price.description: The specific price of the plan version this Organization is billed under. Absent when the plan version carries no price.

scheduled_plan_change.description: Absent when no plan change is pending.

requires_payment_method_to_activate.description: True when this Subscription has never been billed at the gateway yet (still on the platform's $0 default plan) — changing to a paid plan requires a payment method verified via the setup-intent endpoint first.

can_start_new_checkout.description: True when this Subscription is `canceled` — the organization has no blocking subscription and may start an independent new checkout (POST .../billing/subscription/checkout) for any published paid plan, always with a newly collected payment method rather than reusing this Subscription's own (now-ended) one.

subscription.description: Absent when the Organization has no Subscription — a legitimate state for an Organization whose default-plan enrollment failed or that predates enrollment, not an error.

status.description: Absent when the Organization has no Subscription at all — a legitimate state, not an error.

suspended.description: True only for a suspended Subscription. It is the one question the console shell asks, answered here rather than left to every caller to re-derive from `status`.

payment_method_id.description: The payment gateway's own id for an instrument already collected and verified by the browser. No card data is ever sent to this API.

tax_id.description: The organization's tax identifier (e.g. CNPJ in Brazil).

PaymentMethodSummary.description: Identifies a saved instrument without describing it well enough to use. It never carries a full instrument number: `last4` is at most four digits, and there is no other numeric field.

brand.description: The provider's brand label for the instrument (e.g. `visa`), or the method type for an instrument with no brand.

last4.description: Exactly four digits. Omitted for an instrument with no trailing digits to show.

exp_month.description: 1-12. Omitted together with exp_year when the instrument has no expiry.

present.description: False when the Organization has nothing on record — including when the provider no longer holds the instrument it had. A legitimate state the caller renders as an offer to add one, not an error.

amount.description: Integer amount in the currency's smallest unit, never a float.

refunded_amount.description: The gateway-confirmed refunded total, in the same currency. Zero for a charge nothing has been refunded against.

hosted_invoice_url.description: The gateway-hosted invoice for this charge. Omitted — never an empty string — when the gateway published none, so a client renders no link at all rather than a link to nowhere.

receipt_url.description: The gateway-hosted receipt for this charge, omitted on the same terms as `hosted_invoice_url`.

has_more.description: True when the Organization has older charges than this capped page carries.

is_default.description: Exactly one catalog entry carries this flag: the plan every newly provisioned Organization is enrolled into.

prices.description: Every price attached to this plan version. A plan version may carry several simultaneously (e.g. monthly and annual, or the same interval in several currencies).

amount_per_unit.description: An integer amount in the price's currency's smallest unit (e.g. centavos), charged per per_units units of usage beyond the plan's included allowance for this resource.

per_units.description: The block size amount_per_unit is charged per, e.g. 1000 for "R$1,50 per 1000 MTU". Always at least 1. A partial final block is billed as a whole one.

amount.description: An integer amount in the smallest unit of currency (e.g. centavos), never a float. May be 0 — the platform's default plan is a zero-amount plan.

is_default.description: True for the plan's own price for this billing interval, false for a simultaneously published variant (e.g. a pricing-experiment cohort's price). A reader with no assignment of its own renders the default.

overage_rates.description: What usage beyond a metered allowance costs under this price. Empty for a plan version with no metered grant.

policy_limit.description: The included allowance. Absent only when policy_kind is "unlimited".

is_default.description: Exactly one catalog entry carries this flag: the plan every newly provisioned Organization is enrolled into.

prices.description: Every price published against this plan version, not narrowed to one — there is no reading Organization to narrow by. Use is_default to pick the plan's own price per interval.

price_id.description: Must name a price attached to plan_version_id. Required separately because a plan version may carry several prices.
Must name a price attached to plan_version_id. Required separately because a plan version may carry several prices.

payment_method_id.description: A payment method verified through a setup intent (see POST .../billing/setup-intent). Always required: checkout always collects a new payment method, even for an organization whose prior Subscription is canceled — it never reuses one.

limit.description: Present only for a finite policy.

included_amount.description: Present only for a metered or capped-metered policy.

period.description: Present only for a metered or capped-metered policy.

active_count.description: 0 for a metered grant, which has no allocations to count.

client_secret.description: The payment gateway's setup-intent client secret. The frontend confirms it directly against the gateway; it never reaches this API again.

project_id.description: Auto-captured by the console when the Member is viewing a Project-scoped screen; omitted otherwise.

category.description: Required when kind is "ticket"; must be omitted for "feedback".

status.description: Present only for kind "ticket" — a feedback entry's internal status is never exposed.
The ticket's status after this message was applied — reflects an auto-reopen when a Member replied on a resolved ticket.

ticket_id.description: Set when the attachment targets a ticket/feedback entry directly. Exactly one of ticket_id/message_id must be set.

message_id.description: Set when the attachment targets a later reply. Exactly one of ticket_id/message_id must be set.

size_bytes.description: Declared size; re-validated against the real object at confirm time.

object_key.description: Server-derived from the Organization, the owning ticket or message and this attachment_id. Informational only: the confirm endpoint derives it again from the recorded upload and accepts no object key of any kind.

upload_url.description: Presigned URL the client PUTs the object's bytes to directly.

ticket_id.description: Optional. When set it MUST match the owner recorded when the upload was presigned; it is compared, never used to address anything. A value that disagrees is refused as a not-found.

message_id.description: Optional. Compared against the recorded owner exactly like ticket_id.
